questionText:
A rectangular paper sheet of dimensions $54\text{ cm} \times 4\text{ cm}$ is taken. The two longer edges of the sheet are joined together to create a cylindrical tube. A cube whose surface area is equal to the area of the sheet is also taken.

Then, the ratio of the volume of the cylindrical tube to the volume of the cube is
explanation:
Step 1: Find the dimensions and volume of the cylindrical tube.
The rectangular sheet has dimensions $54\text{ cm} \times 4\text{ cm}$.
The two longer edges ($54\text{ cm}$) are joined together to form the cylinder. This means:
• The circumference of the circular cross-section of the cylinder is equal to the shorter edge: $2\pi r = 4\text{ cm} \implies r = \frac{2}{\pi}\text{ cm}$.
• The height of the cylinder is equal to the longer edge: $h = 54\text{ cm}$.

The volume of the cylindrical tube is:
$V_{\text{cylinder}} = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^2 \times 54 = \pi \times \frac{4}{\pi^2} \times 54 = \frac{216}{\pi}\text{ cm}^3$.

Step 2: Find the dimensions and volume of the cube.
The total surface area of the cube is equal to the area of the sheet.
• Area of the sheet $= 54 \times 4 = 216\text{ cm}^2$.
Let $a$ be the side length of the cube.
Total surface area of cube $= 6a^2 = 216 \implies a^2 = 36 \implies a = 6\text{ cm}$.

The volume of the cube is:
$V_{\text{cube}} = a^3 = 6^3 = 216\text{ cm}^3$.

Step 3: Calculate the ratio of the volumes.
$\text{Ratio} = \frac{V_{\text{cylinder}}}{V_{\text{cube}}} = \frac{216/\pi}{216} = \frac{1}{\pi}$.

Therefore, option (A) is correct.
